| **Toggle Side Panel** | Command / keybinding | Closes/opens the **whole** side pane (editor + detail together) → chat-only and back. The mechanics live on the workbench layout service (`toggleSidePane`); while the editor area is maximized, the shared `Workbench.toggleSidePane()` remembers maximization, un-maximizes, then performs the collapse so the restored detail is also hidden. Reopening restores the complete side-pane composition before re-maximizing the editor. Hiding a focused side pane moves focus to the sessions list. |

| **Toggle Sessions List** | Title bar / command | Collapses/opens the left sessions list. Collapsing it gives the freed width to the editor/detail side pane (not the chat); reopening restores the previous editor/detail width so the chat gets that space back. No desktop editor or detail action changes this visibility. |

| **Grid sash** | Between the chat and the third pane | Dragging the side pane never changes Details visibility. Details keeps its minimum width while editor content yields and eventually collapses under width pressure. Dragging a detail-only side pane wider keeps the editor content closed. Double-clicking with Details visible preserves the current Details width and splits all remaining width equally between chat and editor content, with no 600px cap. Grid minimum widths take precedence in narrow layouts. Hiding Details after a reset leaves the chat/side-pane boundary unchanged and returns the Details width to Editor content. With Details hidden the sash uses the native equal split, and in detail-only mode it resets Details to 300px. |

+- **Side chat** — with `sessions.experimental.sideChatsInSidePane` (off by default), each side chat, such as one started with `/btw`, shows as a tab of its own (`ChatEditorInput`, without its session header or Session Activity Bar), while the chat it came from stays in the grid. Opening a side chat (`/btw`, Ask in a Side Chat, the session header's **Side Chats** menu, or **`+` Side Chat**, which asks for the question) is an explicit open, which reveals a closed side pane. Each owner of the side pane's editors (the focused chat, or session, of the grid) has its own side chat tabs: they close when another owner's working set shows and reopen behind its active editor, as its last tabs in the order they had, when the owner's does, also after a reload as their chats load. The side chat tab that was active when the owner was last shown, or the window last saved its state, is active again unless the user chose another editor since, and reveals a closed side pane only if the editor area showed it then. A side chat opened while the grid moves to another owner joins the side chats of the owner it was opened for. Closing a side chat tab closes it for its owner; Details-only collapse keeps its live chat in the hidden editor group. A side chat tab stays in the main window's side pane, and has no detail panel; its chat is read once its tab shows while the editor area does. Other chats started from a side chat tab, such as forks, open in the grid. While the active chat has side chats, including those of its side chats, the Session Activity Bar shows one entry for them after Canvas: it opens the only side chat, or a submenu of them, and is checked while the side pane shows a side chat.

The **auto-managed** tabs (the pinned Changes tab and the default File tab) are opened under `suppressEditorPartAutoVisibility()` — they **never reveal the editor content**. Only a user action (opening an actual file/diff, or dragging the sash) reveals the editor.

@@ -93,7 +93,8 @@ A session host (`ISessionHost`) is a surface that shows a chat: the main window,

- **Lookups.** `ISessionHostService` finds hosts by id, window, editor group, chat, or session, returning the innermost match, and tells whether any host shows a session or chat. It has no selection. Which pane of the grid is the active one, and which panes are detached, only the grid knows: `ISessionsService.getPaneOfHost` gives the pane a host stands for (the active pane for the grid host, a view's pane for the host of a view of the grid, none for other hosts), and `isActivePane` and `isDetachedPane` answer for a host. `getHostOfSession` uses them to pick, of the panes of a window that show a session, the active one, else the one that is not detached.

- **Focused host.** `IFocusedSessionHostService` is the window host that last gained focus; it stays while the app is in the background. Only window-independent consumers, such as voice, use it; UI uses the host it is in.

- **Command targets.** `resolveSessionCommandTarget` resolves what a command acts on: a host its toolbar or menu passes (`createHostMenuOptions`), an editor or window context, a chat, or a session. Without arguments, it resolves the focused host. Arguments that name something that is not found resolve to `undefined`, and the command does nothing; it never falls back to the focused host. Commands of the main window's grid act on the grid's active pane (`ISessionsPartService.getActiveSessionView()`), and neither run nor match their keybindings while a chat window is the focused host.

-- **Chat-host openers.** A surface outside the grid that shows chats, such as a chat window, registers an `IChatHostOpener`. Opening, revealing, opening beside, closing, and activating a chat it shows go through its opener; the grid is not touched. A new chat opened with a reference chat that such a surface shows, such as a side chat, `/btw` or a chat fork, opens beside that chat through the same opener, whatever its origin.

+- **Chat-host openers.** A surface outside the grid that shows chats, such as a chat window, registers an `IChatHostOpener`. Opening, revealing, opening beside, closing, and activating a chat it shows go through its opener; the grid is not touched. A new chat opened with a reference chat that such a surface shows, such as a side chat, `/btw` or a chat fork, opens beside that chat through the same opener, whatever its origin, unless the opener does not open it there (`opensBeside`): it then opens as if no surface showed the reference chat. An opener may also claim chats it does not show yet, as the surface such chats show in (`claimsChat`, resolved with `IChatHostOpenerService.getOpenerFor`): opening a claimed chat reveals it there instead of in the grid.

+- **Side chats in the side pane.** While `ISideChatPlacementService.inSidePane` (the `sessions.experimental.sideChatsInSidePane` setting, in the desktop layout), the main window's side pane shows side chats as editor tabs, and claims them through its opener. The grid holds the side chats of the sessions it shows out of its chat tabs with `hideChatFromGrid`, whether the side pane shows them or not, and never restores one as a session slot's chat; it shows the nearest chat the side chat came from instead (`showAncestorInstead`). Side chats in detached panes of their own stay there. Only side chats open beside a side chat the side pane shows; other chats started from one, such as forks, open in the grid. Each owner of the side pane's editor working set has its own side chats, which close and reopen as the working set of their owner does, and open as their chats load after a reload. A side chat of a chat that a chat window shows opens beside it there.

- **New sessions in chat windows.** A chat window can show a new-session composer as a chat editor, which holds its drafts in a draft slot of its own (`INewSessionDraftHost`). New Session in a chat window (its command, its key while the chat window has focus, and the Sessions picker of the window) opens one as a tab of the window's active chat, or beside it, and shows the active one instead while that is unsent. It starts from the active chat's session: its workspace (including a Dev Container environment), agent, model and mode, and its custom group in the sessions list; the user can change them before sending. Until its session is sent, it stays in its window (moving it to the main window or another window is refused with the reason) and does not take the main window's global composer actions, such as tours or the workspace selection, nor Voice Mode, which keeps addressing the main window's composer. A foreground send turns the tab into the session's main chat in place, held out of the grid like the window's other chats. A background send keeps the tab a composer, reseeded with the same target: the session it starts shows only in the sessions list, and the composer's Open Session link opens it beside the composer. A failed background send gives its prompt back to the composer, or offers it in a notification. An unsent composer restores with its window after a reload, with its input.

- **Grid exclusion.** A chat that a chat window shows is held out of the grid with `ISessionsService.hideChatFromGrid`, while that window shows it. The session leaves the grid when that was the only chat it showed there.

- **Grid host.** `ISessionsService.gridHost` is the main window's host, which shows the grid's active pane. It is the one instance that `ISessionHostService` registers for the main window. The grid's own selection is internal to `ISessionsService`; others read the hosts.

List presentation state is profile-scoped user state, kept in the storage of the window's own profile: the editor window's Sessions view does not share it with the Agents window. This includes grouping, sorting, filtering, section and nested-session collapse, the show more or show less choice of each capped workspace, repository, or environment section, the Chats section, and custom group, pins, automation sessions shown in the list, custom groups with their nesting, automatic-section parents and mixed child order, manual sort keys, and top-level section order. A nested session starts expanded, and the user's later collapse or expansion choice persists across list and window recreation. Storage keys are private implementation details; other components change list state through the owning service API.
